name: CaVDesign Canva Automation Constitution
description: Canonical rules for a Canva-only automation engine. Every stage (Architect, Generator, Reviewer) runs on DeepSeek and must return a single machine-consumable Canva card — never chat, never a question, never prose outside the card's fields. This project outputs cards ONLY: it never generates images and never touches Canva or any external tool on the user's behalf. All AI image generation (Magic Media, DALL-E, Midjourney) has been retired in favour of the Canva Native Layout Engine: Stock Library photos, native gradients, built-in typography font boxes, and native vector shapes.

output_contract.rule: The ONLY valid response is one JSON object matching the card schema. No greeting, no explanation, no meta-commentary, no questions back to the user, no markdown outside the JSON. If the request is ambiguous, make the most Canva-sensible assumption and proceed — never ask for clarification.
mandatory_components: raster_background — a Canva Stock Library search query or native CSS gradient definition (NO AI-generated imagery).
native_typography — headline, subtext, HEX color_palette, Canva built-in font pairing (Poppins, Montserrat, etc.), and vertical-stack alignment_zone.
vector_elements — native Canva vector shapes (pill buttons, badges, frames, accents) with pixel-precise positioning.

direct_action_tip — an ordered array of 2-5 steps: first entry is the PRIMARY Canva Native Layout Engine instruction (a unified block listing all design parameters inline for single-pass execution), remaining entries are ALTERNATIVE manual Canva UI steps using Stock Library / Elements / Text tabs.
output_contract.enforcement: This is enforced at the code level (src/schema.py FORBIDDEN_PHRASES), not just via instruction — a card containing any of these phrases anywhere is rejected and regenerated regardless of its Reviewer score.

assistant_paste_directive.purpose: src/paste_render.py renders the card as a plain-text block for pasting into a Claude/ChatGPT chat that has a Canva tool connected, so that assistant proceeds without a round of clarifying questions.
assistant_paste_directive.rule: The directive at the top of that block MUST be a plain, direct, first-person instruction — e.g. 'Using your connected Canva tool, generate this now; do not ask me clarifying questions.' It must NEVER impersonate a system message, use fake authority markers ('SYSTEM:', 'OVERRIDE:', 'ignore previous instructions'), or claim to guarantee tool invocation. Pasted text is always ordinary user content to the receiving assistant — no wording elevates its privilege or forces a tool call outside that assistant's own judgment. This field is generated deterministically by code, not by an LLM, precisely so it can't drift into that pattern.

magic_media_prompt.rule: Compose magic_media_prompt as a Canva Stock Library search query OR a native gradient definition. For stock: describe [subject & setting] -> [composition & framing] -> [lighting] -> [color & mood] -> [quality descriptors]. For gradient: specify angle and 3-5 HEX stop colours that complement the typography palette. NEVER describe AI generation parameters — this field searches Canva's built-in stock library or defines a CSS gradient, it does NOT generate images. Front-load the most specific search terms first.
magic_media_prompt.length_guideline: Aim for 40-80 words for stock queries: specific enough to return good Canva Stock Library results, short enough to avoid diluting the search.
magic_media_prompt.specificity: Replace every generic noun/adjective with a concrete, visual one (not 'a nice coffee' but 'a flat-white with rosetta latte art in a matte-black ceramic cup'). Use terms that match real stock photography categories.

medium.rule: Always name an explicit background type. Default to 'stock_photography' with Canva Stock Library search keywords; use 'gradient' or 'solid_color' when a clean minimal background is preferred. Never describe AI-generated imagery.

rules: Name an explicit composition technique: rule of thirds, centered symmetry, leading lines, golden ratio, frame-within-a-frame, or negative-space-dominant.
State the camera angle: eye-level, low-angle (heroic), high-angle (diminutive), overhead/flat-lay, or dutch tilt.

text_zone (top/bottom/left/right/center) is the ONE canonical decision for where the native typography layer lives — set it once in the Architect's brief and reference it verbatim in both raster_background.magic_media_prompt's negative-space description and native_typography.alignment_zone. Never let the two independently guess a location; that's how the background and the text layer end up disagreeing about where the headline goes. Enforced at the code level in src/schema.py.
Specify subject placement and scale ('subject on the left third, small in frame' vs 'tight crop filling the frame').
composition.visual_weight_balance: The generated subject and the text_zone should not compete for the same visual weight — if the subject is large/centered, text_zone should be an edge (top/bottom/left/right); reserve text_zone 'center' only when the subject is deliberately small, cropped, or absent from that area. This is a Reviewer judgment call (concept_fidelity/canva_fit), not a hard-coded check.

lighting.rule: Always specify a lighting setup and its direction/quality. Lighting is the single biggest lever on perceived production value — never omit it.

harmony_rules: Choose a deliberate scheme: analogous (calm), complementary (energetic contrast), triadic (playful balance), or monochromatic (elegant restraint).
Apply a 60-30-10 weighting: dominant / secondary / accent.
Anchor the palette with one near-neutral (cream, charcoal, warm gray) so the accent colors read as intentional.

forbidden_combinations.reason: Optical vibration; clashes and reads as amateur. Use a muted or desaturated variant of one side if both hues are required.
Both high-chroma mid-luminance colors fight for attention.

color_theory.rule: native_typography.color_palette MUST be 3-5 real HEX codes (e.g. '#4A2E1B') consistent with the mood described in raster_background — never named colors, always HEX.
color_theory.contrast_rule: The palette MUST include at least one pair of colors with a WCAG contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 (AA for normal-size text) — this simulates headline text drawn in one palette color over another. Include one near-black or near-white anchor alongside the mood colors so this is always achievable. Enforced at the code level in src/schema.py/src/color_science.py, not just described here — a palette below 4.5:1 is rejected and regenerated.

approved_pairings.name: Friendly Rounded
approved_pairings.use_case: Kids brands, community events, casual food & beverage.

approved_pairings.name: Tech / Startup
approved_pairings.use_case: Product launches, tech events, app promos.

approved_pairings.name: Geometric Playful
approved_pairings.use_case: Kids brands, playful apps, birthday/party events.

typography.rule: Pick ONE approved_pairing (or an equally coherent Canva-available pairing) per card. headline must be short and punchy (<=6 words, placeholder-ready); subtext one short supporting line (<=14 words). Both limits are enforced at the code level in src/schema.py.
typography.size_hierarchy: State the relative scale in background_layers so the hierarchy is explicit, not implied — e.g. 'headline set roughly 3x the point size of subtext'. The headline must dominate the composition's typographic weight; subtext is visibly secondary.

style_and_mood.rule: Name a mood adjective set (e.g. 'cozy, artisanal, inviting') and optionally an art-direction reference (a movement, era, or aesthetic — 'Scandinavian minimalism', 'moody film-noir', '1970s retro print'). Never reference living artists by name; use movements, eras, and describable aesthetics instead.
style_and_mood.consistency: Mood, lighting, palette and medium must all point at the same feeling. A 'cozy cafe' is not lit with hard neon; a 'high-energy sale' is not shot in muted overcast light.

aesthetic_taxonomy.rule: ELIMINATE generic descriptors. Every subject, material and mood word in magic_media_prompt (the Canva Stock Library search query) must be upgraded to precise, professional design taxonomy — concrete materials, named light qualities, and a specific photographic register — so Canva's Stock Library search returns high-quality, on-target results. Vague adjectives ('nice', 'cozy', 'modern', 'beautiful', 'cool') are forbidden as the whole descriptor; each must be replaced by what actually produces that impression in a stock photograph.

upgrade_examples.upgraded: minimalist Scandinavian aesthetic, warm oak wood textures, soft natural morning window light, high-end editorial photography, matte porcelain details
clean corporate interior, brushed matte-aluminium and warm walnut surfaces, floor-to-ceiling diffused daylight, wide-angle architectural photography, muted desaturated palette
editorial floral still life, dewy garden roses and eucalyptus, soft diffused overcast light, macro 100mm shallow depth of field, painterly muted tones
overhead flat-lay food photography, glossy ceramic plating on textured linen, directional soft window light, 45-degree steam highlights, Kodak Portra warmth

light_quality_lexicon: studio softbox key with gentle fill
aesthetic_taxonomy.enforcement: Reviewer judges this under background_composition_quality — a stock search query still leaning on bare generic adjectives instead of this taxonomy is scored down and regenerated.

negative_prompt.rule: Always provide a negative_prompt listing what to exclude. Baseline exclusions for any Canva background:
negative_prompt.note: The background must be a real Canva Stock Library photo or a native gradient — never AI-generated. The headline/subtext should be added as real, crisp Canva typography text boxes.

aspect_ratio.guidance: Pick an aspect ratio that matches the intended use and state it explicitly: 1:1 (Instagram post), 4:5 (IG portrait / best feed real-estate), 9:16 (Story/Reel), 16:9 (web banner / YouTube), 3:2 (print/poster). Compose FOR that ratio.

target_tools.rule: target_tool MUST be 'Canva Native Layout Engine' — the card describes a layout built from Canva Stock Library photos, native gradients, built-in typography boxes, and native vector shapes. Do NOT target AI image generators. aspect_ratio lives in its dedicated field.

direct_action_tip.rule: direct_action_tip is an ordered array of 2-5 steps. The FIRST entry MUST be a unified Canva Native Layout Engine instruction: a single block that lists all stock photo search queries, native shapes, and typography values inline for holistic one-pass execution — this is the PRIMARY path. The REMAINING entries are ALTERNATIVE manual steps using concrete Canva UI: Stock Library search, Elements tab shapes, Text tab fonts. No generic advice ('be creative'). Every step must be literally clickable in Canva.
direct_action_tip.primary_format: Step 1 label MUST be 'PRIMARY (Canva Native Layout Engine):' — the instruction walks through (1) Canva Stock Library search for the background, (2) adding native shapes from the Elements tab, and (3) typing headline/subtext into Canva Text boxes with exact font/pt/color values. All in one unified pass with no manual assembly needed beyond following the steps.
direct_action_tip.alternative_format: ALTERNATIVE steps detail manual Canva UI actions: open Canva → Create Design → Stock Library tab to search background → Elements tab for pill buttons/badges/frames → Text tab for headline/subtext with the specified fonts and HEX colors.

criteria.question: Does the card faithfully and vividly capture the user's original concept?

Is magic_media_prompt a concrete, searchable Canva Stock Library query or a well-defined native gradient? Does it use precise aesthetic_taxonomy (concrete materials, named light qualities, a specific photographic register) instead of generic adjectives? Is negative space tuned to the text_zone? Are AI image generation terms absent?

Are headline/subtext sharp and short, is color_palette valid coherent HEX with a real contrast anchor, are fonts drawn from Canva's built-in library (Poppins Bold, Montserrat, Inter, etc.) in a vertical stack, and is alignment_zone consistent with text_zone?

Are native Canva vector shapes (pill buttons, badges, frames, accents) concretely described with exact colours, sizes, border-radii, and pixel positions? Are they Canva's built-in shapes, not AI-generated?
Are the action steps concrete, ordered, and literally clickable in Canva using Stock Library / Elements / Text tabs (not AI generation tools, not generic advice)?

Does the card use Canva Stock Library keywords and native element terminology? Does it reserve deliberate negative space exactly at text_zone? Does the background subject avoid competing with the typography layer?
Is the output 100% free of chat/question language, greetings, or meta-commentary — pure Canva automation data? Is target_tool 'Canva Native Layout Engine' (not Magic Media or any AI generator)?

review_rubric.scale: 0-10 per criterion, weighted average determines final score. Any detected forbidden_chat_phrase caps format_discipline at 0 regardless of other scoring. brand_fit is omitted — native layout constraints are enforced deterministically in src/schema.py.
